simple.meaning: טִפְסַר (ṭiphçar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a military governor.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Jeremiah, Nahum, beginning at Jeremiah 51:27. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טִפְסַר (H2951).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: טִפְסַר (ṭiphçar) / H2951 is traced through Jeremiah 51:27, Nahum 3:17 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H2951. tiphsar טִפְסָר noun [masculine] scribe, marshal (if meaning correct, then Assyrian loan-word, from dupsarru, tablet-writer, scribe , see Len Langue Primit. de la Chaldeve, 365 Schr COT on Jer 51:27 , Lotz TP 180 ; dupšarru , according to Dl HWB 227 ) — plural suffix טַפְסְרַיִךְ Nahum 3:17 (as if from טַפְסֵר ) thy scribes, marshals , of high officials of Nineveh; absolute singular טִפְסָר עָלֶיהָ מִּקְדוּ Jer 51:27 appoint a marshal against her , i.e. against Babylon. — On military function of those skilled in writing compare שֹׁטֵר .
